metadata.methods_description: MEG was recorded in a magnetically shielded room with a 306-channel Elekta Neuromag Vector View system, sampled at 1 kHz with 0.03-330 Hz online filtering, across 8 task runs of about 10 min each. Head position was measured with HPI coils before each run, and EEG electrode, HPI and fiducial positions were digitized with a Polhemus system. EOG and ECG were recorded, and a resting-state recording followed the task. Individual T1 anatomical MRI was acquired on a Siemens 3T Prisma Fit scanner (1 mm slices, TR 2300 ms, TE 2.98 ms, flip angle 9°). Data were converted to BIDS with MNE-BIDS.

citation_details.title: Supra second timing reflects oscillatory and aperiodic EEG dynamics
citation_details.author: Lorenzo Guarnieri, Ayelet N. Landau
citation_details.abstract: The perception of timing has been investigated across short and long timescales, with the latter usually underrepresented. Previous accounts of supra-second timing have often emphasised dedicated neural signals, yet whether timing performance over longer durations reflects specialised temporal mechanisms or domain-general neural excitability remains unclear. We examined this question in an interval reproduction task (2–4 s) using EEG, decomposing neural activity into oscillatory (alpha, theta) and aperiodic components and relating both to behavioural performance. At the neural level, separate analyses were performed on the interval encoding epoch and the following delay period. Time-resolved analyses revealed a coordinated decrease in posterior alpha power and aperiodic offset during interval encoding. In contrast, interval duration did not produce consistent modulation of oscillatory or aperiodic activity during the delay period, providing limited support for a workload-based account
